decisions.reason: As a supplement line close to the existing portfolio, it is cheap to carry and still preserves upside for the firm’s consumer-health expansion, so the option value likely exceeds the cost of keeping it.

This skin-and-hair supplement is a niche but adjacent product with limited carrying cost, so despite uncertain demand a growing pharma firm would usually keep it as a relatively low-risk portfolio option.

Joint-health supplements fit the established consumer-health offer and appear to have received continued support after launch, which makes retention more likely while sales potential remains only partly resolved.

Although somewhat more specialized, this immune supplement is still close to the firm’s supplement range and inexpensive to maintain, so management would likely keep the option open rather than exit quickly.

The generic blood-pressure product is more distant from the core offer and already showed a quality-related problem, so the downside is clearer and the higher regulatory and reputational carrying costs make withdrawal more likely.

The OTC migraine triptan is a more distant bet, but with no clear negative signal yet and plausible strategic value for portfolio broadening, management would slightly favor keeping the option alive for another year.
